newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Bus hijacker frees last hostages, flees to Chechnya.
newsitem.headline: Bus hijacker frees last hostages, flees to Chechnya.

text.p: A hijacker who seized a crowded bus in the south Russian region of Dagestan on Monday freed his last two hostages and fled across the border into Chechnya, Interfax news agency quoted local officials as saying.

Earlier the man had freed up to 48 people and taken off with a local politician and his driver in the politician's car. Interfax said he released these two near the Dagestan border town of Khasavyurt. Earlier conflicting reports had spoken of two or three hijackers but officials contradicted them.
The man, who was reported to be armed with a grenade, had demanded $100,000 ransom and a helicopter after being challenged by police around 6.30 p.m. (1430 GMT).

Little more than an hour later he had exchanged all the hostages -- between 35 and 48 according to various accounts -- for a member of the regional assembly, Gadzhi Makhachev, who had offered himself as a substitute. Dagestan officials said they were sure the hijacker or hijackers were Chechens.

Last January, Chechen separatist guerrillas took hundreds of hostages in the Dagestan town of Kizlyar and then withstood days of Russian bombardment in the village of Pervomaiskoye, near Khasavyurt, before escaping back across the Chechen border.

But Monday's incident appeared non-political. It may have been unplanned but, if premeditated, it was reminiscent of several hijackings before the war in Chechnya, when small groups of Chechens held up buses for ransom in neighbouring regions.
